title.narrative: CASA Cooperation in the Service of Learning in Côte d'Ivoire
CASA Cooperazione al Servizio dell’Apprendimento in Costa d’Avorio

description.narrative: Il progetto CASA Cooperazione al Servizio dell’Apprendimento ha luogo nei Comuni di Treichville, Cocody, Anyama e Koumassi, Abidjan, Costa d’Avorio e mira a fornire risposte concrete alla povertà educativa diffusa a livello nazionale attraverso la creazione di un’alleanza educativa tra gli attori locali (Istituzioni Governative, OSC locali, reti di aziende) e le scuole primarie e secondarie (di primo e secondo livello) con il fine di ampliare l’accesso all’offerta educativa inclusiva e contenere la dispersione scolastica dei ragazzi/e a rischio. Il partenariato di progetto è composto da FADV (OSC capofila) e VIS (OSC italiana) in ATS, Salésiens de Don Bosco, REMAR-CI, ONG Femmes de Valeurs, RESAFEL, Ecole Pratique de la Chambre de Commerce Ivorienne (EPCCI). Vanta inoltre la partnership con il della Donna, Famiglia e Bambini (MFFE) ivoriano e con la Camera di Commercio Ivoriana (CCI). L’intervento dura 36 mesi e raggiunge 11.730 beneficiari diretti totali. L’obiettivo generale, in linea con UN OSS 4 e OSS 8 e le linee guida della Cooperazione Italiana, è di contribuire a migliorare il sistema educativo ivoriano per offrire a tutti i bambini/e ragazzi un’istruzione e una formazione di qualità, equa e inclusiva, in grado di generare opportunità di inclusione sociale e benessere. La strategia portante del progetto, esplicitata nell’obiettivo specifico, è di creare un’alleanza educativa tra i diversi enti locali e le 20 scuole nei quattro comuni designati, volta a promuovere un modello di scuola che qualifichi l’istruzione come apprendimento, che lavori sulle competenze trasversali e che si appropri della trasformazione digitale con un focus su tematiche di genere, disabilità e bisogni educativi speciali, e che offra ai giovani più vulnerabili concrete opportunità di crescita scolastica, sociale e professionale basate su uguaglianza e equità, in linea con il Plan Sectoriel Education/Formation 2016-2025 del governo Ivoriano. Il modello di alleanza in sviluppo a livello globale valorizza il partenariato nell'apprendimento continuo, la creazione di reti educative tra scuole e privato, e la progettazione di piani e politiche pubbliche per una scuola inclusiva sempre più condivisa. L’intervento verte su tre componenti principali che rispecchiano i risultati attesi, quali: 1. Miglioramento della governance locale e attuazione di un piano di adeguamento infrastrutturale per gli istituti scolastici. Azioni previste: i) creazione di Tavoli di Lavoro Municipali ii) Istituzione del Manager di comunità; iii) adeguamento infrastrutturale delle scuole (interventi WASH ed efficientamento energetico); iv) Avvio e modernizzazione di laboratori digitali, classi IT, Atelier professionali e rinforzo del Centro per bambini sordo muti di Koumassi e delle Classi Speciali presso la Scuola Remar ad Anyama. 2. Riduzione dei fenomeni di dispersione scolastica (bocciature, ripetenze e abbandoni) e analfabetismo. Azioni previste: i) Formazione per insegnanti su metodologie di insegnamento efficace e percorsi di educazione digitale per studenti; ii) Rinforzo delle competenze disciplinari degli studenti in procinto di accedere al livello scolastico successivo; iii) Workshops socio-educativi per genitori, studenti e insegnanti su tematiche trasversali; iv) Percorsi formativi per lo sviluppo delle competenze trasversali e l'orientamento (PCTO), v) Corsi di alfabetizzazione per soggetti non scolarizzati. 3. Potenziamento dei meccanismi di transizione scuola-lavoro (riduzione mismatch) con l’adozione di offerte professionalizzanti per i giovani nei settori ad alta richiesta. Azioni previste: i) Mobilità di studenti tra Costa d'Avorio e Ghana in seno al programma formativo sulle energie rinnovabili; ii) attivazioni nuovi corsi professionalizzanti presso la EPCCI iii) Erogazione tirocini per studenti dei licei tecnico-professionali con la CCI; iv) Formazione per studentesse su gestione aziendale.

The project CASA (Cooperation for Learning Service) takes place in the municipalities of Treichville, Cocody, Anyama, and Koumassi in Abidjan, Ivory Coast. It aims to provide concrete solutions to the widespread educational poverty at the national level by creating an educational alliance among local actors (Government Institutions, local CSOs, business networks) and primary and secondary schools (both first and second level) with the goal of expanding access to inclusive education and maximizing efforts to reduce school dropout rates for at-risk children. The project partnership is composed of FADV (leading NGO), VIS (Italian NGO), Salesians of Don Bosco – REMAR CI – NGO Femmes de Valeurs, RESAFEL, Ecole Pratique de la Chambre de Commerce Ivoirienne (EPCCI). It also boasts partnerships with the Ivorian Ministries of Women, Family and Children (MFFE) and the Ivorian Chamber of Commerce (ICC). The intervention lasts 36 months and reaches a total of 11.730 direct beneficiaries. The overall objective, in line with the UN SDGs 4 and 8 and the guidelines of Italian Cooperation, is to contribute to improving the Ivorian educational system in order to provide all children and youth with quality, equitable, and inclusive education and training that generates opportunities for social inclusion and well-being. The main strategy of the project, as outlined in the specific objective, is to create an educational alliance between the different local entities and 20 schools, aimed at promoting a school model that qualifies education as learning, focuses on transversal skills, embraces digital transformation without losing sight of gender issues and the needs of students with disabilities and special educational needs, and offers the most vulnerable youth concrete opportunities for academic, social, and professional growth based on equality and equity, in line with the Ivorian government’s Plan Sectoriel Education/Formation 2016-2025. The alliance model, emerging globally enhances the continuous learning perspective of the partnership, networking and educational projects within-and-between schools and the private sector, and the development of work plans and public policies for increasingly concerted inclusive education. The intervention focuses on three main components which reflect the expected results, such as: 1. Improvement of local governance and implementation of an infrastructure adjustment plan for schools. Actions include: i) creation of Municipal Working Groups; ii) establishment of Community Managers; iii) infrastructure adjustments in schools (WASH and energy efficiency); iv) Launch and modernization of digital laboratories, IT classrooms, vocational training workshops, and strengthening of the Koumassi Deaf-Mute Children's Center and the Special Classes of Anyama Remar’s school. 2. Reduction of school dropout phenomena (failures, repetitions, and dropouts) and illiteracy. Actions include: i) specific teacher training on effective teaching methodologies and digital education pathways for students; ii) reinforcement programs for students’ disciplinary skills in preparation for the next school level ; iii) educational projects for parents, students, and teachers to impact health, environmental education, and respect for differences; iv) co-designing educational pathways for students with teachers, focusing on transversal skills and career orientation (PCTO); v) basic literacy courses for non-schooled individuals. 3. Enhancement of school-to-work transition mechanisms (reduction of mismatch) with the adoption of professional training opportunities for youth in high-demand sectors. Actions include: i) student mobility between Ivory Coast and Ghana as part of a training program on renewable energy; ii) introduction of new vocational courses at EPCCI; iii) internships for students; iv) professional training for female students in business management.

tag.narrative: Build and upgrade education facilities that are child, disability and gender sensitive and provide safe, non-violent, inclusive and effective learning environments for all
By 2030, achieve full and productive employment and decent work for all women and men, including for young people and persons with disabilities, and equal pay for work of equal value
By 2030, ensure that all girls and boys complete free, equitable and quality primary and secondary education leading to relevant and effective learning outcomes
By 2030, ensure that all girls and boys have access to quality early childhood development, care and pre-primary education so that they are ready for primary education

By 2030, ensure that all learners acquire the knowledge and skills needed to promote sustainable development, including, among others, through education for sustainable development and sustainable lifestyles, human rights, gender equality, promotion of a culture of peace and non-violence, global citizenship and appreciation of cultural diversity and of culture’s contribution to sustainable development
By 2030, ensure that all youth and a substantial proportion of adults, both men and women, achieve literacy and numeracy
By 2030, substantially increase the number of youth and adults who have relevant skills, including technical and vocational skills, for employment, decent jobs and entrepreneurship

By 2030, substantially increase the supply of qualified teachers, including through international cooperation for teacher training in developing countries, especially least developed countries and small island developing States
Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all
Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all
